extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi and 1 MPa = 10 bar, so 0.1 MPa is about 15 psi, 0.15 MPa about 22 psi, 0.2 MPa about 29 psi, 0.5 MPa about 73 psi, 0.6 MPa about 87 psi, 0.7 MPa about 101 psi (7 bar), 0.8 MPa about 116 psi and 1 MPa about 145 psi (10 bar). Temperature: -5 deg C is 23 deg F and +40 deg C is 104 deg F.

A pressure range such as 0.15 MPa to 0.7 MPa on a pilot-operated solenoid valve gives the lowest pressure at which the valve shifts reliably and the highest it may be used at; the upper figure is the maximum operating pressure and the lower figure is a minimum, not a rating.
extraFacts.source: SMC valve catalogue specification tables (operating pressure range); ISO 4414

extraFacts.fact: A 3-way valve has 3 ports and 2 positions; a 4-way or 5-port valve has 4 or 5 ports and 2 positions; a 3-position 5-port valve adds a centre position. All ports blocked (closed centre) holds a cylinder, centre exhaust vents both cylinder ports and pressure centre pressurises both. A single-solenoid valve returns when de-energised; a double-solenoid 2-position valve stays in its last position. A manifold base carries several valves on common supply and exhaust passages and is closed with blanking plates where a station is unused.
extraFacts.source: ISO 1219-1 (fluid power graphical symbols); Indus Hydraulics guide 'Solenoid valve functions explained: 3/2, 5/2 and 5/3 valves'

extraFacts.fact: A solenoid coil is built for one supply type and voltage; a coil on the wrong voltage or supply type will not switch the valve and can burn out.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414 (pneumatic fluid power, general rules and safety requirements)

extraFacts.fact: Cv is a flow coefficient: the higher the Cv, the more air a valve passes at a given pressure drop.
extraFacts.source: ANSI/ISA-75.01.01; Indus Hydraulics guide 'Sizing pneumatic valves: Cv, Kv, sonic conductance'

extraFacts.fact: Customs classification: valves and parts of valves fall under HS heading 8481.
